articles.title: FAA let contractors work w/o approval before ground stop: Sources
articles.titleZh: 消息人士称，在停飞令下达之前，FAA允许承包商在未经批准的情况下开展工作
articles.summary:
On the morning of last week’s historic nationwide ground stop, an FAA technician escorted a private contractor from L3Harris into a remote radio communications site for air traffic control centers in south Arkansas, to replace a decades-old router.

The FAA technician believed his role ended when the contractor entered the facility. He went about his own work without knowing exactly what the L3Harris engineer was doing, according to two sources familiar with what happened in the room, and the union that represents FAA technicians.

0:00 What the FAA is saying about the contractors' work
3:15 Is the administration being transparent enough?
4:34 Is there a crisis with US leadership? A panel debates.

articles.readingText:
On the morning of last week’s historic nationwide ground stop, an FAA technician escorted a private contractor from L3Harris into a remote radio communications site for air traffic control centers in south Arkansas, to replace a decades-old router.

The FAA technician believed his role ended when the contractor entered the facility.

He went about his own work without knowing exactly what the L3Harris engineer was doing, according to two sources familiar with what happened in the room, and the union that represents FAA technicians.
articles.readingTextZh:
上周发生历史性的全国航班停飞的那个早晨，一名联邦航空管理局（FAA）的技术人员陪同L3Harris的一名私人承包商前往阿肯色州南部的空中交通管制中心的一个远程无线电通信站点，更换一台使用了数十年的路由器。

FAA技术人员认为，当承包商进入设施时，他的职责就结束了。

据两位熟悉该房间内情况的消息人士以及代表FAA技术人员的工会称，他忙于自己的工作，并不确切知道L3Harris工程师在做什么。
